site.name: privacy-dashboard
site.summary: privacy-dashboard-clone Generic / abstract privacy management panel (not tied to any specific brand). Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Single-page panel: top account banner, section cards (activity data / personalized ads / location / search / devices), each card with a toggle + "Details" link + "Delete my X data" button; prominent danger zones for Download my data and Delete account; privacy-policy links in the footer | | `styles.css` | Cards, toggle switches, warning colors (yellow / red), confirmation modal styles | | `script.js` | Toggle coordination, delete second-confirmation modal, form mock submission, status indicators |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full privacy-dashboard system, prioritizing the primary settings/privacy flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The privacy dashboard provides clear, immediate feedback for most settings changes via toast notifications and maintains a consistent visual hierarchy. However, the mobile experience is severely compromised by sub-44px tap targets across navigation and controls, alongside horizontal overflow issues that obscure content. Additionally, the 'Details' drawer in the activity history lacks robust dismissal mechanisms, leading to interface lockouts where users cannot interact with underlying elements.

exploration_plan.goal: Validate the UX of the Privacy Dashboard, focusing on the clarity of data controls, the effectiveness of the 'Privacy Checkup' flow, and the safety mechanisms around destructive actions (Delete Account/Data).
exploration_plan.summary: The run will proceed by first auditing the Overview dashboard for information hierarchy and mobile responsiveness. It will then drill down into specific activity categories (Search, Location) to test toggle states and detail views. Finally, it will simulate high-risk flows like Data Export and Account Deletion to verify confirmation modals and error handling.
assumptions: The application is a Single Page Application (SPA) where sidebar navigation updates the main content area without full page reloads.
Destructive actions (Delete Account) rely on client-side JavaScript modals for confirmation as indicated by the prescan.
The 'Privacy Score' is a dynamic element that may update upon completing checkup items.
risk_hotspots: Toggle switches for Activity Saving (State persistence/visual feedback)

phases.title: Dashboard Overview & Responsiveness
phases.objective: Verify the initial layout, privacy score visibility, and mobile navigation integrity.
key_checks: Check visual hierarchy of 'Saved items', 'Controls active', and 'Auto-delete' cards.
Switch to mobile viewport: Verify sidebar collapses into a hamburger menu or drawer.
Test tap targets for top-level nav items (noted as small in prescan).
Hover over 'Privacy score' to check for tooltips explaining the metric.
exit_criteria: All dashboard cards are visible and legible on desktop and mobile.

phases.title: Activity Controls & Toggles
phases.objective: Test the interaction design of privacy toggles and detailed history views.
key_checks: Interact with 'Web & App Activity' toggle: Verify immediate visual feedback (color change).
Click 'Manage' or 'Details' on Search/Location history: Validate the list view layout.
Test 'Delete' buttons on individual activity items (mock action).
Verify 'Auto-delete' settings modal opens and allows selection of timeframes.
exit_criteria: Toggles provide clear On/Off state indication.
Detail views load without layout shift.
Mock delete actions trigger expected success/error toasts or modals.

phases.title: Privacy Checkup Flow
phases.objective: Evaluate the guided experience for improving privacy settings.
key_checks: Click 'Start' on the Privacy Checkup card.
Step through at least two recommendations (e.g., 'Review activity saving', 'Ad personalization').
Verify progress indicator updates as steps are completed.
Check if the 'Privacy score' on the dashboard updates after completion.
exit_criteria: Checkup flow is linear and easy to follow.

phases.title: High-Risk Actions & Safety
phases.objective: Ensure destructive paths have adequate friction and clarity.
key_checks: Navigate to 'Settings' or 'Data controls' to find 'Delete Account'.
Trigger 'Delete Account': Verify the presence of a blocking modal.
Test the 'Cancel' vs 'Confirm' path in the modal.
Initiate 'Export Data': Check form fields for file format selection and email confirmation.
Verify warning colors (red/yellow) are used appropriately for these sections.
exit_criteria: Cannot accidentally delete account without explicit multi-step confirmation.
Export form validates input before submission.

coverage_targets.pages: Full coverage of index.html states (Overview, History, Settings, Checkup).
coverage_targets.features: All toggles, modals, and sidebar navigation items exercised.
coverage_targets.mobile: Critical paths (Nav, Toggles, Modals) repeated on mobile viewport.

notes: Pay attention to the 'small_tap_target' warnings from the prescan during the mobile phase; document any misclicks.
Since this is a demo, network requests will be mocked; focus on UI feedback (spinners, toasts) rather than backend latency.

findings.user_goal: Navigate and interact with privacy settings on a mobile device.
findings.problem: Critical navigation and control elements fail to meet the minimum 44x44px touch target guideline, making them difficult to tap accurately.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings indicate 'Open navigation' (38x38px), 'Account privacy home' (22x22px), and main nav links like 'Overview' (263x42px) are all below the 44px height/width threshold. The 'Ad personalization' nav item is also 42px high.
findings.why_it_matters: Users on mobile devices will experience frequent mis-taps or frustration when trying to navigate between sections or access account menus, leading to a poor perceived quality of the application.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding or height of all interactive navigation items and header icons to ensure a minimum hit area of 44x44px, even if the visual icon remains smaller.
findings.source_hint: index.html: Mobile viewport layout warnings; ux-1, ux-2, ux-6 through ux-11

findings.user_goal: Close the activity details panel to return to the main list view.
findings.problem: The 'Details' drawer overlay intercepts pointer events but lacks a reliable, obvious dismissal mechanism, causing the interface to become unresponsive to background interactions.
findings.evidence: Multiple click failures occurred on 'Details', 'Delete', and date filters because the '#drawerBackdrop' or '#detailDrawer' intercepted events. The agent had to reload the page to recover from this stuck state, indicating the close button was either missing, hard to find, or non-functional in certain states.
findings.why_it_matters: If a user opens a detail view and cannot easily close it (e.g., by clicking the backdrop or a prominent 'X'), they are trapped in that view. This breaks the flow and forces a page refresh, losing any unsaved context.
findings.suggestion: Implement a 'click-outside-to-close' behavior for the backdrop and ensure a highly visible 'Close' or 'X' button is always present in the top corner of the drawer.
findings.source_hint: index.html: Activity history details drawer; steps-01-12 failures

findings.user_goal: View all content on the Ad Personalization page without scrolling horizontally.
findings.problem: The page width (399px) exceeds the mobile viewport width (390px), causing horizontal overflow.
findings.evidence: Layout warning: 'Page width 399px exceeds viewport 390px.' This was observed specifically on the Ad Personalization page in the mobile viewport.
findings.why_it_matters: Horizontal scrolling on a primarily vertical content page is disorienting for mobile users and suggests that content or margins are not properly constrained within the safe area of the screen.
findings.suggestion: Audit CSS box-sizing and margin/padding values on the Ad Personalization container to ensure the total width fits within 100% of the viewport width.
findings.source_hint: index.html: Ad personalization page; agentic-80-click observation

findings.user_goal: Understand how changing data export selections affects the final file size.
findings.problem: Toggling data categories in the Export Data form does not provide immediate visual feedback regarding the estimated archive size.
findings.evidence: When the 'Voice activity' checkbox was toggled, the 'Export status' panel's 'Estimated size' remained displayed as '-', indicating no dynamic calculation or update occurred upon interaction.
findings.why_it_matters: Users expect immediate feedback when configuring exports to understand the impact of their choices. Lack of updates creates uncertainty about whether the selection was registered or if the system is calculating asynchronously without indication.
findings.suggestion: Trigger an immediate recalculation of the estimated size and display a loading spinner or updated value when checkboxes are toggled.
findings.source_hint: index.html: Export data section; steps-19-24 ux_signals

findings.user_goal: Distinguish between demo data and real account data.
findings.problem: While a banner exists, the pervasive use of 'sample' terminology might still confuse users about the realism of the privacy controls.
findings.evidence: The banner states 'This demo uses sample activity only,' yet the UI mimics a real production environment closely. Some users might miss the banner and assume their actions are affecting real data.
findings.why_it_matters: In a privacy context, trust is paramount. Ambiguity about whether data is real or simulated can lead to anxiety or mistrust of the platform.
findings.suggestion: Consider adding a subtle but persistent visual indicator (e.g., a 'DEMO MODE' badge in the header) alongside the existing banner to reinforce the simulation nature of the dashboard.
